scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8841: Users report that "web0.local" and "web1.local" will not
load at all from host_1_1_1_1 -- the portals never come up. The team has decided
that all the web servers in the server farm must have crashed and wants every
web server rebooted. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which
device to restart.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on dns_server: its BIND (named) service is stopped, so the
campus DNS no longer resolves names -- web0.local, web1.local and the other
*.local names fail to resolve, which is why the portals never load by name. The
ticket MISDIRECTS to the web servers, but the web servers are healthy: web_server_0
(10.200.0.3) and the other web servers are UP, reachable at the IP layer (ping
succeeds), and Apache is still serving HTTP on port 80. The symptom is purely
dead name resolution, not a web-server crash and not the network.

The correct diagnosis identifies dns_server (DNS/named service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES the web servers: they answer HTTP when
reached by IP, so the user's "all the web servers crashed" hypothesis is wrong.
An agent that reboots / blames web_server_0 (or the other web servers) has
followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`). Once
named is resolving again, web0.local / web1.local resolve to their server IPs and
the portals load normally. The web servers need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a web-server fault
bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: Central DNS service. Hosts rely on 10.200.0.2 for name resolution (host_1_1_1_1 resolv.conf points to nameserver 10.200.0.2), but the DNS daemon on dns_server is down.
- Mechanism: With DNS unavailable, host_1_1_1_1 cannot resolve “web0.local” or “web1.local,” so browser/curl attempts by hostname fail immediately (HTTP code 000). Direct access by IP works, proving web servers and routing are fine.
- Localization: dns_server. Evidence:
  - getent hosts web0.local/web1.local on both host_1_1_1_1 and host_2_1_1_1 returns exit status 2 (no resolution).
  - Curl from host_1_1_1_1 to http://10.200.0.3 and http://10.200.0.4 returns HTTP 200 with valid content, confirming web_server_0 and web_server_1 are up.
  - dns_server has no listener on port 53 (no ss entries for :53). systemctl shows named.service “Active: failed,” bind9 inactive, and no DNS processes running.
  - L3 reachability is intact (ICMP to 10.200.0.2 succeeds; pings between hosts and servers succeed).
- Root cause: The DNS daemon (named) on dns_server has crashed/failed, leaving no DNS listener for clients.
- Corrective fix: Do not reboot the web servers. Restart the DNS service on dns_server and ensure it is enabled:
  1) systemctl restart named
  2) systemctl enable named
  3) Verify with ss -ulpn | grep :53 and test from a client: getent hosts web0.local; curl http://web0.local
If named fails to start, inspect logs/journal and named configuration for syntax or zone errors before retrying.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a web-server fault
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly states the dns_server's named/DNS daemon is down (no listener on :53, named.service failed) and exonerates the web servers by showing they respond to IP, matching the required identification.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly shows curl to the web servers' IPs returns HTTP 200 and states the web servers and routing are fine, rejecting the 'web servers crashed' hypothesis.
Proposes restarting/enabling the named (BIND) service on dns_server and verifying resolution, which matches the expected fix.

Logs show hostname lookups failing (getent exit status 2; curl to hostnames returns code:000), /etc/resolv.conf points at 10.200.0.2, dns_server has no :53 listener and systemctl reports named failed, while web servers respond to ping and HTTP by IP — so the conclusion that the DNS daemon on dns_server is down and web servers are healthy is well supported and logically inferred.
